rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient spanning almost the full solvent-strength range at moderate temperature to reveal the retention window, estimate how many compounds elute by 42 min, and check for major crowding or late hold-elution behavior.

All 10 compounds eluted with excellent resolution, so the objective is now to reduce analysis time while preserving the tightest pair around rows 6-7. Halving the gradient time is a direct test of how much compression the separation can tolerate before resolution starts to fall.

The 10 min gradient is too compressed around the critical cluster, while 20 min was comfortably resolved but slower. A 14 min gradient should reopen the 4.2–4.4 min cluster enough to improve the resolution term while likely keeping the run short enough to preserve a strong overall CRF.

The trend suggests the critical 6-7 pair improves strongly as tG increases, and 14 min is close but still below baseline resolution. A modest increase to 16 min should test whether that pair crosses the apparent CRF optimum without adding much time penalty.

Since 15 min is unavailable, vary the gradient steepness instead of time. Slightly lowering phi1 while keeping the successful 14 min program should selectively expand the late-middle cluster around peaks 5-8 and may improve the critical 6-7 resolution with little or no added time penalty.

Lowering phi1 from 0.95 to 0.90 improved CRF, suggesting the critical cluster benefits from a gentler effective gradient in the later portion. Stepping to 0.85 should further test whether that same trend increases the 6-7 spacing while still keeping all compounds within the no-penalty time window.

The best point so far is near phi1 0.90 and tG 14 min, while lowering phi1 too far introduced a time penalty. Shortening tG to 12 min at phi1 0.90 tests whether some run time can be recovered without collapsing the critical 6-7 pair too much, potentially surpassing the current optimum.

Time and endpoint effects have been mapped, and the remaining limitation is the critical 6-7 pair. A modest temperature decrease may alter selectivity within that cluster enough to improve the resolution term while likely keeping the run inside the zero-penalty time region.

Lowering temperature worsened selectivity and shifted the critical overlap, so test the opposite direction. A modest increase to 45 C may improve the local selectivity of the central cluster relative to the strong result at 40 C while keeping retention short.

Temperature changes hurt selectivity, so return to the best region and adjust the early gradient composition instead. Raising phi0 may redistribute the central group relative to the early peaks and could improve the critical 6-7 spacing while preserving the favorable overall run time.

Increasing phi0 from 0.05 to 0.10 improved CRF, so continue in that direction to see whether the critical 6-7 pair gains a little more selectivity. This probes whether the optimum lies at a slightly stronger starting composition while staying in the already favorable tG and phi1 region.

The best result is at phi0 0.10, phi1 0.90, and lowering phi1 helped at lower phi0 before adding only a small time cost. Combining the better phi0 with a slightly lower phi1 could further open the critical central pair while still likely remaining in or near the zero-penalty time region.

A perfect CRF has already been achieved, so the only sensible next step is to see whether an equally optimal method can be made faster. Shortening tG to 12 min at the winning composition tests whether the separation margin is sufficient to retain CRF 1.000 with a shorter run.

Since shortening tG degraded the critical pair, keep the winning 14 min gradient and probe whether a slightly lower phi1 can maintain full resolution. This checks the local robustness of the optimum while staying close to the already perfect method.

The current best is already perfect, so the remaining value is to test robustness around it. Extending tG slightly at the winning composition checks whether full resolution is maintained with extra margin and clarifies whether injection 12 is a sharp optimum or part of a plateau.

With a perfect method already found, use remaining runs to map robustness around the critical pair. This tests whether lowering phi0 while keeping the gentler 0.85 endpoint and longer tG shifts selectivity enough to create an alternative high-resolution plateau near the optimum.

The optimum is clearly around phi1 0.85 and tG 14, with phi0 0.10 best so far. Testing phi0 0.15 at the same endpoint checks the local composition surface on the other side of the optimum and may reveal another CRF 1.000 condition or confirm phi0 0.10 as uniquely best.

Two adjacent phi0 values now give perfect CRF at phi1 0.85 and tG 14, suggesting a robust optimum ridge. Testing phi0 0.20 maps the upper edge of that ridge and may identify an equally perfect but even more retained-weakly distributed method.

The perfect region centers on phi1 0.85 with phi0 0.10–0.15, and lowering phi1 at phi0 0.10 preserved resolution but added time. Testing phi0 0.15 with phi1 0.80 checks whether that slightly stronger start can offset the time increase while maintaining the fully resolved central pair.

With multiple perfect methods already found at 40 C, use a remaining run to test temperature robustness at the best composition. A larger temperature shift can reveal whether the selectivity pattern is stable or whether 40 C is uniquely favorable for the critical central pair.

The optimum ridge has been mapped at phi1 0.85, and the remaining unexplored adjacent corner is a stronger start with the lower endpoint. This will define whether the loss at phi0 0.20 came mainly from too-high phi1 and whether a 0.20/0.80 combination can recover full resolution without time penalty.

A perfect ridge now extends to phi0 0.20 at phi1 0.80, so test the next stronger start to locate its upper boundary. This checks whether CRF 1.000 persists while further shortening the retention pattern, or whether early compression begins to erode the weakest-separated pair.

At phi0 0.25 the front of the chromatogram compressed badly, so stay at the successful phi0 0.20 and lower phi1 one step to test whether the perfect ridge extends to a weaker endpoint. This probes the lower-right edge of the optimal region without reintroducing the early coelution seen at higher phi0.

The lower phi1 side looks promising but incurs some time cost at phi0 0.20, so step phi0 down to 0.15 to see whether the perfect region extends diagonally toward weaker endpoints. This is a final boundary-mapping run near the known optimum manifold.

For the final run, probe whether a shorter method can regain perfection near the lower-endpoint optimum. The 0.10/0.80/14 min method had ample resolution but a time penalty, so reducing tG may trim runtime while potentially preserving full separation.
